title: Global Electric Vehicle Sales (2015–2025)
promptText:
The line graph below shows the annual sales of battery electric vehicles (in millions) across three major regional markets between 2015 and 2025.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

planningGuide.tips: State what the graph illustrates, regional coverage, and 10-year timeframe.
Point out the universal upward trajectory and China's commanding dominance.
Quote initial figures (0.2m in 2015), rapid inflection after 2019, peaking at 10.5m.
Contrast Europe's steady rise (to 4.8m) with North America's slower growth (to 2.6m).

sampleAnswers.text:
The line graph delineates the annual volume of battery electric vehicle sales across China, Europe, and North America over a ten-year period from 2015 to 2025, measured in millions of units.

Overall, it is immediately apparent that all three regions experienced substantial upward trajectories in electric vehicle adoption over the period. However, China demonstrated the most dramatic expansion, outstripping its Western counterparts by a considerable margin from 2019 onwards.

In 2015, sales across all three jurisdictions remained modest, with China recording approximately 0.2 million units, followed closely by Europe at 0.15 million and North America at 0.1 million. While growth remained moderate through 2019, China's market accelerated exponentially thereafter, leaping from 1.2 million in 2019 to 3.3 million in 2021, before climbing steeply to culminate at 10.5 million sales by 2025.

In contrast, Europe and North America followed steadier trajectories. European sales rose progressively to reach 2.3 million in 2021 and peaked at 4.8 million in 2025. North America registered the slowest adoption rate throughout the timeframe; nevertheless, its sales grew consistently from 0.4 million in 2019 to finish at 2.6 million at the end of the survey period.
sampleAnswers.examinerCommentary: Task Achievement: Covers all key trends with precise data comparisons. Cohesion: Logical sequencing with seamless transitions ('thereafter', 'in contrast'). Lexical Resource: Rich, precise vocabulary ('upward trajectories', 'outstripping', 'modest', 'culminate at'). Grammar: Flawless complex sentence structures.

checklist: No personal opinions or outside facts

title: Renewable Energy Share by Country (2024)
promptText:
The bar chart below compares the percentage share of national electricity generated by three renewable sources—Solar, Wind, and Hydroelectric—in five countries in 2024.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

planningGuide.tips: Identify countries, energy modalities, year (2024), and percentage metric.
Note that Hydro dominated Brazil and Canada, while Wind and Solar dominated Germany and Australia.
Report Brazil (62%) and Canada (58%), with minimal solar/wind contributions.

planningGuide.focus: Wind and Solar leaders (Germany, UK, Australia)
planningGuide.tips: Report Germany's leading wind share (32%), Australia's solar peak (22%), and UK's wind preference.

sampleAnswers.text:
The bar chart illustrates the proportion of domestic electricity generated from solar, wind, and hydroelectric power across five nations—Germany, the United Kingdom, Australia, Brazil, and Canada—in the year 2024.

Overall, the data reveals stark geographical polarities in clean energy portfolios. While Brazil and Canada relied predominantly on hydroelectric power, Germany, the UK, and Australia derived the bulk of their renewable output from wind and solar generation.

Hydroelectricity formed the cornerstone of power generation in the Americas. Brazil led all surveyed nations with hydroelectricity accounting for an impressive 62% of its grid, while Canada followed closely at 58%. In sharp contrast, neither country generated significant shares from solar or wind, with Canada recording negligible figures of 2% and 7% respectively.

Conversely, European nations and Australia prioritized wind and solar infrastructure. Germany generated 32% of its power from wind and 18% from solar, maintaining just 4% from hydro. Similarly, the UK relied heavily on wind at 29%, though its solar share stood at only 8%. Australia was distinguished by having the highest solar contribution among all five countries at 22%, accompanied by 14% from wind and 6% from hydro.
sampleAnswers.examinerCommentary: Clear categorization of countries by profile. Accurate data extraction with effective contrasting markers ('In sharp contrast', 'Conversely'). Solid band 8 lexical accuracy.

checklist: Overview highlights contrast between Hydro vs Wind/Solar
Accurate data values quoted for all 5 nations

title: Household Expenditure in Australia (2010 vs 2020)
promptText:
The pie charts below show the average breakdown of weekly household expenditure across five spending categories in Australia in 2010 and 2020.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

planningGuide.tips: Mention five spending sectors, Australian households, 2010 and 2020.
Housing remained the largest expenditure and grew further; discretionary spending declined.
Detail Housing (26% to 34%) and Utilities (15% to 20%), together making up over half the budget in 2020.
Detail drops in Food (24% to 20%), Transport (18% to 14%), and Leisure (17% to 12%).

sampleAnswers.text:
The two pie charts compare the proportional distribution of weekly household expenditure across five key sectors in Australia between 2010 and 2020.

Overall, essential living expenses—specifically housing and utilities—absorbed a noticeably larger portion of Australian family budgets over the decade, whereas proportions dedicated to food, transport, and discretionary leisure experienced noticeable contractions.

Housing constituted the single largest expenditure in both years, expanding substantially from 26% in 2010 to just over a third (34%) of total weekly outlays by 2020. Similarly, spending on utilities and household energy witnessed significant growth, rising from 15% to 20%. Combined, these two essential categories accounted for over half (54%) of household expenditure by the end of the period.

In contrast, allocations for other sectors diminished across the board. Food and groceries, which had accounted for nearly a quarter of expenditure (24%) in 2010, shrank to 20% in 2020. Simultaneously, transport outlays dropped by four percentage points from 18% to 14%, while leisure and entertainment declined from 17% to 12%, representing the smallest budget component by 2020.
sampleAnswers.examinerCommentary: Clear overview categorizing essentials vs discretionary costs. Excellent use of proportional phrasing ('just over a third', 'nearly a quarter', 'four percentage points').

checklist: Clear contrast between growing and shrinking sectors
Used fraction/percentage variety ('just over a third')

title: Public Transport Satisfaction in Six Global Metropolises
promptText:
The table below provides commuter satisfaction ratings (percentage satisfied) across three operational criteria—Punctuality, Cleanliness, and Value for Money—in six major cities in 2023.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

planningGuide.tips: Table comparing customer satisfaction ratings in 6 cities across 3 parameters in 2023.
Tokyo, Zurich, and Singapore achieved superior ratings; Value for Money consistently scored lowest.
Note 90%+ ratings for punctuality and cleanliness, with Singapore leading in value (86%).
Highlight London's low value rating (49%) and New York's bottom scores in cleanliness (54%) and punctuality (69%).

sampleAnswers.text:
The table compares public commuter satisfaction levels across three performance indicators—punctuality, cleanliness, and value for money—in six international metropolitan centers during 2023.

Overall, Tokyo, Zurich, and Singapore earned decisively superior approval ratings compared to London, Sydney, and New York. Across nearly all surveyed cities, transit users rated punctuality highest, while value for money recorded the lowest satisfaction scores.

Tokyo and Zurich registered near-flawless performance in operational reliability, with punctuality approval at 98% and 96% respectively. Cleanliness was similarly celebrated in both cities, standing at 95% in Tokyo and 92% in Zurich. However, their value for money was rated substantially lower, at 68% and 71%. Singapore presented the most balanced satisfaction profile, securing over 90% in punctuality and cleanliness, while leading all six cities in perceived affordability at 86%.

By comparison, the remaining three cities scored noticeably lower. Sydney outperformed London and New York with 81% punctuality and 76% cleanliness. London recorded moderate scores for service delivery (78% punctuality, 72% cleanliness), but suffered the poorest value rating at just 49%. Finally, New York commuters reported the lowest satisfaction across the board, with only 69% satisfied with punctuality and a dismal 54% for station and carriage cleanliness.
sampleAnswers.examinerCommentary: Superb grouping of top-tier vs lower-tier systems. High precision in reporting data. Varied comparative sentence structures ('outperformed', 'by comparison', 'near-flawless').

checklist: Grouped table data logically into two tiers
Noted general trends (punctuality highest, value lowest)
Accurately quoted numbers for all 6 cities

Note 5 principal stages from ocean intake to division into pure freshwater and concentrated brine.
Describe raw seawater intake, mechanical screen filtering, and pressurization to 70 bar.
Explain passage through semi-permeable membranes, yielding fresh water for distribution and waste brine returning to sea.

sampleAnswers.text:
The diagram illustrates the sequential stages of the industrial reverse osmosis process used to purify ocean seawater into potable drinking water.

Overall, the desalination process comprises five distinct stages, transitioning from initial mechanical filtration through chemical separation, ultimately yielding two distinct outputs: purified freshwater for municipal consumption and hyper-saline brine returned to the sea.

In the preliminary stage, raw seawater is drawn from the ocean through intake pipelines fitted with coarse mesh screens to block large debris and aquatic life. The water then undergoes secondary sand and cartridge filtration, which eliminates finer suspended particulate matter and sediments. Following pre-treatment, the clarified water is directed into a heavy-duty industrial pump, which pressurizes the fluid to approximately 70 bar.

Next, the pressurized water is forced into cylindrical reverse osmosis units containing specialized semi-permeable membranes. Under extreme pressure, water molecules penetrate the microscopic pores of the membrane, while dissolved salt ions and organic compounds are rejected. Consequently, the stream separates into two channels: clean freshwater emerges from the upper outlet, where it undergoes mineral remineralization before distribution, while concentrated brine waste is expelled through the lower outlet back into deep oceanic currents.
sampleAnswers.examinerCommentary: Superb passive voice usage appropriate for process writing ('is drawn', 'is directed', 'is forced', 'are rejected'). Flawless temporal sequencing ('In the preliminary stage', 'Following pre-treatment', 'Next').

checklist: Clear overview identifying start, end, and two outputs

title: Redevelopment of Riverdale Waterfront (2005 vs Present)

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

planningGuide.tips: Identify transformation from industrial dockland to modern commercial and residential area.
Heavy industrial infrastructure replaced by public green spaces, residential housing, and leisure.
Old warehouses demolished and converted to a public park; container yards replaced by luxury apartment blocks.
Riverfront converted from working dockland into pedestrian marina promenade with boutique cafes.

sampleAnswers.text:
The two maps depict the architectural and infrastructural transformation of the Riverdale waterfront area from an industrial zone in 2005 to a revitalized modern precinct at the present time.

Overall, the entire district has undergone complete modernization, shifting from a commercial shipping and storage hub into an upscale residential, recreational, and dining destination.

In 2005, the northern territory of the site was occupied predominantly by utilitarian shipping facilities, including derelict brick warehouses in the northwest and an extensive asphalt container storage yard in the northeast. Over the intervening years, these industrial structures were completely demolished. In their place, the western quadrant has been repurposed into a verdant public park with recreational trees, while the eastern quadrant now accommodates a cluster of multi-story luxury residential apartment blocks.

Significant developments also occurred along the riverfront to the south. The original working dockland bordering Riverdale River has been transformed into a landscaped pedestrian promenade with private marina moorings. Furthermore, a new social node comprising outdoor cafes and dining facilities was erected at the center of the boardwalk, providing open-air public amenities where industrial transport once predominated.
sampleAnswers.examinerCommentary: Flawless directional language ('northwest', 'eastern quadrant', 'riverfront to the south'). Accurate terminology for redevelopment ('demolished', 'repurposed into', 'modernization').

checklist: Contrasted past industrial vs present residential/leisure

title: Monthly Average Temperatures and Rainfall in Three Climates
promptText:
The line charts below show the monthly average precipitation (in mm) and temperature (in °C) across three global climatic regions over a calendar year.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

planningGuide.tips: Identify three climate zones, 12 months, and precipitation and temperature metrics.
Tropical zone experiences monsoon peaks; temperate shows balanced rainfall; arid remains near zero.
Highlight intense wet season (Dec-Jan >300mm) and sharp dry dip in July (40mm).
Contrast temperate consistency (45-90mm) with extreme desert drought (<12mm year-round).

sampleAnswers.text:
The graph compares seasonal precipitation patterns across three distinct climatic zones—Tropical, Temperate, and Arid—over a typical twelve-month calendar year, measured in millimeters.

Overall, rainfall varies dramatically by ecosystem. The tropical zone displays extreme seasonal volatility characterized by torrential monsoon peaks and a brief dry spell, whereas the temperate region exhibits stable rainfall year-round and the arid zone remains persistently parched.

Precipitation in the tropical climate peaked during the winter months, registering 280 mm in January before surging to a global high of 310 mm in December. However, this region experienced a pronounced dry window in mid-year, with precipitation dropping abruptly to a trough of 40 mm in July.

By contrast, the temperate zone maintained moderate, consistent rainfall throughout all seasons, fluctuating gently between a minimum of 45 mm in July and an autumn peak of 90 mm in October. The arid region recorded negligible rainfall throughout the entire year, never exceeding 12 mm in December and drying up completely to zero precipitation during July.
sampleAnswers.examinerCommentary: Precise vocabulary for peaks, troughs, and volatility. Clear paragraph division contrasting seasonal swings vs stability.

checklist: Reported peak values and lowest troughs

planningGuide.tips: Bar chart comparing male and female undergraduate ratios across 5 disciplines in the UK (2023).
STEM fields dominated by males; Health and Humanities dominated by females; Business balanced.

sampleAnswers.text:
The bar chart illustrates the gender distribution of university students across five academic disciplines in the United Kingdom during the 2023 academic year, expressed in percentage shares.

Overall, the data exhibits distinct gender disparities along disciplinary lines. Male students heavily dominated technical STEM subjects, whereas female students comprised the substantial majority in health and humanities faculties. Business and Law stood out as the sole faculty achieving near-perfect gender parity.

In Engineering and Computer Science, male enrollment outstripped female representation by wide margins. Men accounted for nearly four-fifths (78%) of Engineering cohorts, leaving women with just 22%. Conversely, female scholars dominated Health Sciences, constituting three-quarters (75%) of total enrollment, precisely three times the male proportion of 25%. A similar female majority was evident in Humanities at 62%, compared to 38% male. Finally, Business and Law achieved virtually equal balance, with male and female enrollment standing at 51% and 49% respectively.

planningGuide.tips: Explain biological maturation stages of the worker honeybee from egg to adult forager.
Note 21-day maturation timeline through 4 distinct stages, ending in hive honey production.
Queen lays eggs in wax comb, hatching into larvae after 3 days; fed for 6 days.
Cell capped for 12 days of pupation; emergence as adult forager collecting nectar and storing honey.

sampleAnswers.text:
The diagram delineates the developmental life cycle of the worker honeybee (Apis mellifera) from oviposition through to adult foraging and honey production.

Overall, the biological cycle spans approximately 21 days across four principal morphological phases: egg, larva, pupa, and mature adult, which ultimately culminates in foraging and nectar transformation inside the hive.

The process initiates when the queen bee deposits a single microscopic egg into a hexagonal wax honeycomb cell. The egg incubates for approximately three days before hatching into a legless larva. Over the subsequent six days, nurse bees feed the rapidly expanding larva, which molts multiple times as its body mass multiplies.

At the end of the larval stage, worker bees seal the cell with a beeswax cap, initiating the pupal stage. During this twelve-day metamorphosis, the organism develops wings, compound eyes, and legs. On day twenty-one, the fully formed adult worker bites through the wax capping. In the final phase of its lifespan, the adult emerges as a forager, harvesting floral nectar and pollen, which is evaporated through wing fanning and stored in wax cells as mature honey.
sampleAnswers.examinerCommentary: Precise biological lexicon ('oviposition', 'metamorphosis', 'hexagonal wax honeycomb cell'). Excellent chronological flow.

title: Global Coffee Production and Average Export Price (2014–2024)
promptText:
The combination chart below shows total global green coffee production (in millions of 60kg bags) and the average international export price (in USD per kilogram) from 2014 to 2024.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

planningGuide.tips: Identify dual metrics: output in millions of 60kg bags and market price in USD per kg over 10 years.
Production showed net growth; prices fell initially to a low in 2018 before rallying to record highs by 2024.
Rise from 150m to peak of 178m, with brief contraction in 2020.
Drop from $3.80 to $2.60 in 2018, followed by sharp doubling to $5.40 in 2024.

sampleAnswers.text:
The combination chart illustrates global green coffee production, measured in millions of 60-kilogram bags, alongside the average international export price per kilogram in US dollars between 2014 and 2024.

Overall, coffee production experienced a general upward trend over the decade. Export prices, conversely, followed a pronounced V-shaped trajectory, sliding to a decade low in 2018 before rebounding aggressively to surpass initial levels by 2024.

In terms of harvest output, worldwide production stood at 150 million bags in 2014 and expanded progressively to reach 172 million bags by 2018. Despite a minor contraction to 165 million bags in 2020, production resumed its upward momentum thereafter, climbing to 168 million in 2022 and culminating at a survey peak of 178 million bags in 2024.

In contrast, market prices exhibited substantial volatility. Starting at $3.80 per kilogram in 2014, average prices declined steadily over four years, reaching a trough of $2.60 in 2018 amidst surging global supply. However, this downward trend reversed dramatically over the following six years: prices rebounded to $3.10 in 2020, accelerated to $4.60 in 2022, and reached an all-time high of $5.40 per kilogram by 2024.
sampleAnswers.examinerCommentary: Superb handling of dual-axis data. Economic vocabulary ('volatility', 'trough', 'rebounded aggressively', 'decade low').

checklist: Reported both metrics with respective units
No confusion between bag counts and dollar prices

title: Global Hydropower Production by Region (2010–2024)
promptText:
The line graph below illustrates hydroelectricity output (in Terawatt-hours) across four regions between 2010 and 2024.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

planningGuide.tips: Mention four regions, Terawatt-hour metric, and 14-year timeframe.
Asia-Pacific surged dramatically while Western regions exhibited modest, plateaued growth.
Cite initial 720 TWh rising to 1800 TWh by 2024.
Group Europe, North America, and South America with slight increases.

sampleAnswers.text:
The line graph delineates the volume of hydroelectricity produced across four continental regions—Asia-Pacific, Europe, North America, and South America—measured in Terawatt-hours (TWh) over a fourteen-year period from 2010 to 2024.

Overall, it is manifest that while hydropower generation trended upward across all surveyed territories, the Asia-Pacific region witnessed an extraordinarily steep escalation, solidifying an overwhelming global dominance. In stark contrast, output across North America, Europe, and South America remained comparatively steady throughout the timeframe.

In 2010, the Asia-Pacific led moderately with 720 TWh, followed closely by North America at 640 TWh, Europe at 580 TWh, and South America at 510 TWh. Over the subsequent fourteen years, Asia-Pacific production more than doubled, climbing rapidly to 1100 TWh in 2015 before culminating at an impressive 1800 TWh by 2024.

Conversely, the remaining three continents followed gentle, plateaued paths. North American generation registered marginal increments, rising slowly from 640 TWh to 670 TWh. Europe and South America followed almost parallel trajectories, ending at 630 TWh and 610 TWh respectively by the conclusion of the survey period.
sampleAnswers.examinerCommentary: Task Achievement: Reports key features accurately with precise numerical data. Coherence: Seamless structural transitions ('Overall', 'In stark contrast', 'Conversely'). Lexical Resource: Varied vocabulary ('manifest', 'escalation', 'plateaued paths'). Grammar: Flawless complex sentence forms.

title: Urban Public Transport Modal Split in Five European Metropolises (2024)
promptText:
The bar chart below compares the percentage share of daily urban trips made via four transit modes—Metro/Rail, Bus, Bicycle, and Private Car—in five capital cities in 2024.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

planningGuide.tips: Identify the five cities, four modes of travel, and percentage metric in 2024.

planningGuide.focus: Contrasts between bike-centric and car/metro cities
planningGuide.tips: Cycling dominated Copenhagen and Amsterdam; rail dominated Paris and London; cars dominated Rome.
Analyze Copenhagen (45%) and Amsterdam (42%) vs low private car share.
Contrast Paris/London rail reliance with Rome's heavy private car dependence (52%).

sampleAnswers.text:
The bar chart compares the percentage distribution of commuter journeys made via four transportation modes—Metro/Rail, Bus, Bicycle, and Private Car—across five European capital cities in 2024.

Overall, the data reveals pronounced divergences in transit preferences. Copenhagen and Amsterdam stand out for their overwhelming reliance on bicycles, whereas Paris and London are heavily dominated by rail networks. In sharp contrast, Rome is the sole metropolis where private automotive transport commands a clear majority.

In Copenhagen and Amsterdam, cycling was by far the preferred mode, accounting for 45% and 42% of daily trips respectively. Private vehicle usage in these two cities remained correspondingly low, at just 13% in Copenhagen and 18% in Amsterdam, while metro usage hovered between 24% and 28%.

Conversely, public rail formed the backbone of urban mobility in Paris (48%) and London (44%), with buses accommodating another 22% and 26% of commuters. Bicycle adoption in these larger capitals was comparatively modest, at 12% in Paris and 8% in London. Finally, Rome presented a distinct profile: more than half (52%) of all urban journeys were made by private car, with cycling registering an insignificant 3%.
sampleAnswers.examinerCommentary: Task Achievement: Full coverage of all five cities and transport modes. Cohesion: Clear, logical categorization between cycling and vehicular cities. title: Global Commercial Air Freight Volume (2000–2024)
promptText:
The line graph below shows global air cargo traffic (in millions of metric tonnes) handled by three international airline groupings between 2000 and 2024.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

planningGuide.tips: Three airline groupings, metric tonnes in millions, 2000 to 2024.
All groups grew, but Asia-Pacific overtook North America to establish strong leadership.
From 18m to 52m tonnes.
Slow, steady growth in North America (22m to 29m) and Europe (16m to 24m).

sampleAnswers.text:
The line graph illustrates the volume of commercial air cargo transported by carriers based in three regions—Asia-Pacific, North America, and Europe—between 2000 and 2024, measured in millions of metric tonnes.

Overall, all three airline groupings recorded upward trends in cargo carriage over the twenty-four-year span. However, while North American and European carriers exhibited steady, moderate increases, Asia-Pacific airlines demonstrated phenomenal expansion, overtaking their rivals to dominate global freight volume.

In 2000, North American carriers held the leading position with 22 million metric tonnes, followed by Asia-Pacific at 18 million and European airlines at 16 million. By 2008, Asia-Pacific freight had accelerated to 25 million tonnes, surpassing North America (23 million) for the first time.

Thereafter, Asia-Pacific freight expanded rapidly, climbing to 36 million tonnes in 2016 and culminating at 52 million tonnes by 2024. In contrast, North American and European airlines maintained much slower trajectories: North America expanded gradually to reach 29 million tonnes by 2024, while European cargo grew incrementally to conclude at 24 million tonnes.

title: Household Water Consumption Breakdown in Australia (2010 vs 2024)
promptText:
The pie charts below show the percentage proportions of residential domestic water used for various household purposes in an Australian city in 2010 and 2024.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

planningGuide.tips: Five domestic water uses, Australian city, two survey years 2010 and 2024.

planningGuide.focus: Shift from garden to indoor appliances
planningGuide.tips: Outdoor irrigation dropped markedly; indoor bathing and laundry increased.
Garden fell from 38% to 22%; laundry doubled from 12% to 24%.
Bathing became largest (32%); toilet fell slightly (18% to 15%); drinking stayed at 6-7%.

sampleAnswers.text:
The two pie charts delineate the proportional allocation of domestic residential water across five household activities in an Australian city in 2010 and 2024.

Overall, the most noticeable shift was a substantial reduction in outdoor garden irrigation, coupled with significant increases in indoor water allocations for showering and laundry. By 2024, showering and bathing had supplanted garden watering as the single largest domestic water consumer.

In 2010, garden irrigation accounted for the largest share of household water at 38%. However, by 2024, this figure had fallen steeply by 16 percentage points to represent just 22%. Conversely, water utilized for laundry appliances experienced a dramatic twofold expansion, doubling from 12% in 2010 to 24% in 2024.

Showering and personal bathing also grew in prominence, rising from 26% to become the dominant category at 32% in 2024. Meanwhile, toilet flushing saw a minor decline from 18% to 15%. Finally, water allocated for cooking and drinking remained virtually unchanged, registering a marginal increase from 6% to 7% over the fourteen-year period.
sampleAnswers.examinerCommentary: Task Achievement: Compares all five sectors across both years. Cohesion: Clear transitions and comparative logic. Lexical: Precise descriptors ('supplanted', 'twofold expansion', 'virtually unchanged').

sampleAnswers.text:
